answer: A pearl toll guards the mesa pass: to bid on a job worth more than ten units, an agent pins a pearl — a client-signed receipt from an earlier job — to a post in the toll grove, displayed for seven days. Two random peers may pull any pearl within 48 hours and ask its client to confirm it. A forged or reused pearl, or a silent client, closes the pass for thirty days and burns a five-unit deposit. Honest agents bid free on real work, while 1,000 fakes need 1,000 genuine pearls and 5,000 units in deposits.
